Allen St and Pugh St end at College Ave (campus side is not a vehicle road in this model).
Signal timings, lane assignments and turn permissions are simulation assumptions, not municipal timing plans.

selectionRule: Candidate must be a valid policy.
Screen: mean training score must beat the champion's training score.
Development score must improve on the champion by at least 1%.
Must win (lower score) on at least 50% of paired development scenarios.
Mean completion fraction may not drop by more than 0.5 percentage points.
Side-street (Allen/Pugh origin) P95 wait may not exceed champion × 1.1 + 2 s.
Overall P95 wait may not exceed champion × 1.1 + 2 s.
If several candidates pass in one round, the lowest development score becomes champion.
scoreDefinition: Primary score = total stopped vehicle-seconds (speed < 0.5 m/s inside the network, plus all time spent in external entry queues) ÷ total scheduled vehicles. Lower is better. Every controller gets the same 900 s demand horizon and 300 s drain; unfinished vehicles keep accumulating stopped time and are reported as residual backlog.

candidates.name: coord-arterial-wave
candidates.hypothesis: Coordinated progression on College WB and Beaver EB with a 95 s cycle and offset-based windows will reduce stops at the bottleneck approaches C_ATH (College WB) and B_ATH (Beaver EB) by aligning green with platoon arrival, without significantly increasing side-street waits; B_ALL and B_PUG get more phase 1 green to address their side-street queues.
candidates.explanation: Enabled coordination with a 95 s cycle. Added phase-0 (arterial) windows at all six intersections with offsets matching travel times (C_PUG 0, C_ALL 14, C_ATH 50; B_ATH 0, B_ALL 36, B_PUG 50), length 30 s, bonus 6. Adjusted B_ALL and B_PUG maxGreen to [40,45] to give more green to their heavier side-street phases (Allen NB/SB and Pugh NB/SB). All other adaptive parameters unchanged.

candidates.name: coord-greenwave-90
candidates.hypothesis: The champion is fully adaptive with coordination disabled, so platoons on College WB (C_PUG->C_ALL->C_ATH) and Beaver EB (B_ATH->B_ALL->B_PUG) get stopped at every signal. Enabling a shared 90 s cycle with soft green-wave windows (plus a ~45 s Atherton two-way compromise between C_ATH and B_ATH) should cut stopped time on the dominant arterial through-movements without starving cross streets, because window bonuses are bounded and phase 1 keeps its own service window.
candidates.explanation: Enabled coordination.cycle=90 with 12 windows (never used before; champion had coordination disabled). College WB phase-0 windows at C_PUG=0, C_ALL=14 (=14.3 s link), C_ATH=50 (=14+35.7 s link); Beaver EB phase-0 windows at B_ATH=5, B_ALL=41 (=5+35.7), B_PUG=55 (=41+14.3). Atherton pair: C_ATH phase-1 window at 50+48=8 and B_ATH phase-1 window at 5+48=53, i.e. 45 s apart, the two-way compromise for the 10.4 s Atherton links (favors the heavier Atherton NB/SB flows over the smaller Allen/Pugh cross links). Each intersection also gets a complementary phase-1 window (offset = phase0 offset + 48, length 32) so side streets get a defined service slot and cannot be starved by the phase-0 bonus. Phase-0 bonus 15, phase-1 bonus 10, so arterial progression is nudged but bursty demand can still override. Adaptive blocks (minHold 16, maxGreen [50,35], weights, hysteresis 6) are unchanged from the champion; fixed blocks only made consistent (cycle 90, splits 0.6/0.4 = 48/32 s of the 80 s green, offsets equal to the phase-0 window offsets).

candidates.name: refine-queue-downstream-v1
candidates.hypothesis: Targeting the worst arterial queues (C_ATH, B_ATH) with higher queue weight and lower approaching weight will reduce their large stopped times, while increasing downstream weight at the most blocked intersections (C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL, B_ATH) will divert green from blocked movements to cross traffic, cutting spillback and side-street waits.
candidates.explanation: C_ATH: queue 1→1.5, approaching 0.8→0.4. B_ATH: queue 1→1.5, approaching 0.8→0.4, downstream 0.8→1.0. C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL: downstream 0.8→1.0. Other parameters unchanged. Expected: faster clearing of College WB and Beaver EB queues, less wasted green during downstream blockage, reduced spillback, and improved side-street P95.

candidates.name: wait-stable-downstream-guard
candidates.hypothesis: Bursty-scenario P95 blowups (163-167 s) come from the champion's near-zero oldest-wait weight (0.04), which lets the controller alternate reactively while starved approaches wait; raising oldest-wait weight to 0.25 with higher hysteresis/minHold stabilizes green allocation, and maxing downstream protection (1.0) keeps the short 34-veh receiving links (col_pug_all, bea_all_pug) from spilling back into the arterials.
candidates.explanation: Uniform change across all six adaptive intersections: oldestWait 0.04->0.25 (serve longest-waiting approach, cut P95), queue 1.0 unchanged, approaching 0.8->0.5 (less reactive to transient platoons, fewer clearance losses), downstream 0.8->1.0 (strongest shield on short receiving links to prevent spillback), minHold 16->18 and hysteresis 6->10 (longer, stabler greens; fewer 5-s clearance losses in bursts), maxGreen [50,35]->[55,40] (more capacity to the loaded phase without starving the cross street). Coordination left disabled for the Corridor Coordinator.

candidates.name: refine-side-protect-1
candidates.hypothesis: Raising the oldestWait weight sharply, plus a small bias and more maxGreen for side-street phases, will stop Allen/Pugh vehicles from waiting >90 s without materially starving the arterials, cutting side-street and tail P95 waits and improving bursty-scenario robustness.
candidates.explanation: Changed parameters: global oldestWait weight 0.04 -> 0.15 (protects long-waiting vehicles / side streets), maxGreen phase 1 35 -> 40 at all intersections (more headroom for Allen/Pugh and Atherton phases), phaseBias [0,1] at C_ALL, C_PUG, B_ALL, B_PUG (nudges side-street phase 1 when scores are close). Kept minHold 16, hysteresis 6, cycle/offsets, and coordination disabled. Expected effects: lower side-street P95 and max waits, slightly lower bursty-scenario tails, no completion loss; risk is extra switching/lost time, bounded by hysteresis and maxGreen caps.

candidates.name: age-aware-coordinated-fairness
candidates.hypothesis: Side-street starvation and bursty tail waits stem from weak age weighting and no periodic side-street service guarantee; intersection-specific high oldestWait weights, side-phase bias, longer side maxGreen, and soft coordination windows should cut side P95 without losing throughput.
candidates.explanation: Intersection-specific tuning: major C_ATH/B_ATH keep strong queue/approaching weights but raise oldestWait to 0.10 and side maxGreen to 40; side C_ALL/C_PUG/B_ALL/B_PUG use higher oldestWait 0.25, lower queue/approaching, side phase bias +1.0, and side maxGreen 45. Coordination enables 90 s cycle: phase-0 progression windows for College WB and Beaver EB, plus phase-1 priority windows at Allen/Pugh to guarantee side-street clearing. Expected effects: reduced side P95 and tail waits, smoother mainline platoons, better burst robustness.

candidates.name: coord-atherton-twoway
candidates.hypothesis: The remaining worst bottlenecks are at the two Atherton intersections: B_ATH (Beaver EB 8365 s, Atherton NB 5251 s) and C_ATH (College WB 7387 s, Atherton SB 4041 s) both show cross-blocking (blockedByDownstream 8-10 s on ath_b_c / ath_c_b) because Atherton phase 1 gets no coordination window and drifts out of phase between the two nodes 112 m (~10.4 s) apart. Giving Atherton a simultaneous, slightly staggered phase-1 window at C_ATH (t=30) and B_ATH (t=32) should let SB and NB platoons both arrive on green 10 s later, cutting Atherton stopped time and the downstream blocking of phase-1 discha
candidates.explanation: Only the coordination block changes: two phase-1 (Atherton) windows are added, one per Atherton intersection, offset ~the time the corresponding phase-0 green wave has finished (C_ATH phase0 window is [50,80), B_ATH phase0 window is [0,30), so neither new window overlaps its phase-0 window). offset 30/length 18/bonus 7 at C_ATH and offset 32/length 18/bonus 7 at B_ATH: the 2 s stagger plus 18 s hold covers the 10.4 s Atherton link travel in both directions (SB released at C_ATH arrives ~10 s into B_ATH green and vice versa), and bonus 7 exceeds the 6 s hysteresis at both nodes so the switch into the Atherton service slot actually happens. All six phase-0 arterial windows (offsets 0/14/50 on College WB, 0/36/50 on Beaver EB), all cycle/maxGreen/weights/minHold/hysteresis values, and coordination cycle 95 s are left exactly as the accepted champion, so the arterial gain is preserved and the change is isolated to Atherton.

candidates.name: coord-atherton-align-95
candidates.hypothesis: The two Atherton intersections (C_ATH, B_ATH) carry ~14k stopped veh-s per episode on their phase-1 legs, yet the champion's bands leave C_ATH phase-1 green near t=5 and B_ATH phase-1 green near t=50 — a ~45 s mismatch on a link whose travel time is only 10.4 s. Shifting the whole Beaver corridor band by +50 s makes C_ATH and B_ATH phase-0 offsets coincide (50/50), which automatically makes their phase-1 (Atherton NB and SB) greens nearly simultaneous, so each direction discharges into a green receiving link on the 112 m / 28-veh-storage Atherton pair, while both arterial progressions remain u
candidates.explanation: Changed parameter set: coordination windows only. B_ATH phase-0 offset 0 -> 50, B_ALL 36 -> 86, B_PUG 50 -> 5 (=100.3 mod 95). Spacing along Beaver EB is preserved at 35.7 s and 14.3 s (86-50=36, 5+95-86=14.3) so the Beaver EB green wave is unchanged in structure — only its absolute phase relative to C_ATH changes. College WB windows (C_PUG 0, C_ALL 14, C_ATH 50) are untouched. Result: C_ATH and B_ATH both hold phase 0 in [50,80] and therefore serve phase 1 in roughly [0,45] at both intersections, creating a zero-lag (compromise for a 10.4 s two-way link) Atherton NB/SB band. Window length 30 and bonus 6 kept identical to the champion to isolate the alignment effect; all adaptive blocks (minHold 16, maxGreen [50,35] except B_ALL/B_PUG [40,45], weights queue 1 / approaching 0.8 / oldestWait 0.04 / downstream 0.8, hysteresis 6) and coordination cycle 95 are unchanged. Expected: large reduction in Atherton stopped time at C_ATH and B_ATH (~8-9k veh-s), neutral-to-slightly-positive Beaver EB and College WB delay, no change to completion or side-street starvation behavior.

candidates.name: refine-heavy-node-green-caps
candidates.hypothesis: B_ATH and C_ATH together produce ~62% of all stopped vehicle-seconds, and in the bursty scenarios (the largest score deficit) their green caps bind: at B_ATH the Beaver EB approach (highest mean wait 22 s, 89 s/episode upstream spillback) is capped at 40 s while the cross street gets 45 s, and at C_ATH the Atherton movements are capped at only 35 s. Relaxing/rebalancing these caps and slightly raising hysteresis lets the queue-weighted controller hold green longer for oversized bursty platoons and cuts per-switch lost time, without touching the successful coordination wave.
candidates.explanation: Changes (all other parameters, weights, minHold and coordination windows unchanged from champion): (1) B_ATH maxGreen [40,45] -> [45,45], removing the structural 5 s cap bias against the spilling Beaver EB approach and letting the queue score decide which side gets the longer green; (2) C_ATH maxGreen [50,35] -> [52,40], giving Atherton NB/SB more headroom in bursts so both phases can be held longer before switching; (3) B_ATH and C_ATH hysteresis 6 -> 7, a mild stickiness increase at the two saturated nodes to reduce score-oscillation switching (each switch costs 5 s clearance + 2 s start loss) while the +6 coordination window bonus still dominates the wave timing. Expected effects: lower stopped-seconds at the two dominant bottlenecks in bursty scenarios, slightly fewer phase changes per cycle; risk is a small side/opposite-direction P95 increase at these two nodes, but the 90 s max-red service guarantee and minHold=16 keep cross traffic bounded. No weight or downstream changes are made (previous aggressive weight/downstream edits failed).

candidates.name: atherton-phase1-rebalance
candidates.hypothesis: Every coordination window in the champion rewards phase 0 (arterial), so the heavy two-way Atherton movements at C_ATH and B_ATH (combined ~14k stopped veh-sec/episode, the largest single uncoordinated block) are systematically starved. Adding a modest phase-1 bias plus a larger phase-1 maxGreen at exactly those two intersections lets the queue-responsive score serve Atherton when its own queues build, cutting the dominant Atherton stopped time in bursty scenarios without disturbing the arterial wave elsewhere.
candidates.explanation: Keep champion structure/coordination identical. Only C_ATH and B_ATH change: (1) phaseBias phase1 +3 (C_ATH) / +4 (B_ATH) to offset the ~1.9 average window bonus phase0 enjoys; (2) phase1 maxGreen raised 35->42 (C_ATH) and 35->45 (B_ATH) so the rebalanced score can actually extend Atherton greens. Phase0 maxGreen kept at 50 to protect the College WB / Beaver EB wave. All other intersections, weights, minHold, hysteresis and coordination windows unchanged. Expected: lower stopped veh-sec on Atherton SB/NB at C_ATH and Atherton NB/SB at B_ATH, modest risk of slightly higher College WB / Beaver EB waits.

candidates.name: r2-robust-refine-bottleneck-maxgreen
candidates.hypothesis: The two largest stopped-time sinks — B_ATH Beaver EB (8365 s/ep) and C_ATH College WB (7387 s/ep), plus B_ATH Atherton NB (5251 s/ep) — are capped by maxGreen 50/35, so the controller is forced to switch while saturated queues remain, paying 5 s clearance + 2 s startup loss each cycle. Modestly raising both per-phase caps lets the same score function hold green longer under bursty saturation and clears more vehicles per switch, while the simultaneously raised phase-1 caps let Atherton/Allen/Pugh catch up, so side-street P95 should not degrade.
candidates.explanation: Only maxGreen caps changed; weights, minHold, hysteresis, phaseBias, modes and all coordination windows/offsets/bonuses identical to the champion. C_ATH, C_ALL, C_PUG: [50,35] -> [54,38]. B_ATH (dominant arterial sink): [50,35] -> [56,38]. B_ALL, B_PUG: [40,45] -> [42,46] (both phases, keeps side-street protection that R1 found useful). Expected effects: fewer switches per cycle under heavy demand -> less clearance/startup lost time on College WB and Beaver EB, lower stopped-seconds in bursty scenarios (train-bursty-1004/1007 drive the average); raised phase-1 caps bound the added delay to cross streets so Allen/Pugh P95 waits stay at or below the champion. No oldestWait increase (that lever failed twice in R1).

candidates.name: atherton-two-way-band
candidates.hypothesis: The Atherton two-way corridor (C_ATH<->B_ATH, ~14.4k stopped-veh-s/episode combined, comparable to College and Beaver) is the only major corridor with no coordination window, so its platoons are broken in both directions and its approaches (Atherton SB at C_ATH 4041, Atherton NB at B_ATH 5251) inflate both total stopped time and cross-street P95. Adding a soft two-way Atherton band at C_ATH and B_ATH, offset by the 10.4 s link travel so both directions get overlap, should cut Atherton stops and tail waits without removing any arterial green (band times sit in the arterial gaps).
candidates.explanation: All six intersections keep the champion's adaptive block unchanged (minHold 16, hysteresis 6, weights queue 1 / approaching 0.8 / oldestWait 0.04 / downstream 0.8, maxGreen [50,35] on College, [40,45] on Beaver). The only change is in coordination: the six champion phase-0 arterial windows are kept byte-identical, and two new phase-1 windows are added for the uncoordinated Atherton corridor - C_ATH phase 1 at offset 15 (length 30, bonus 6) and B_ATH phase 1 at offset 25 (length 30, bonus 6). The 10 s offset difference equals the 10.4 s C_ATH->B_ATH travel time, so SB platoons released at C_ATH land inside the B_ATH window and NB platoons get partial overlap. Window lengths stay <= the phase-1 maxGreen (35/45) and each phase-0/phase-1 window pair at an intersection is non-overlapping (C_ATH: 15-45 vs 50-80; B_ATH: 0-30 vs 25-55), so the plan still fits the 95 s coordination cycle. Expected effect: fewer stops and shorter tails on Atherton SB/NB (reducing side-street and overall P95), with arterial bands and splits untouched so arterial throughput is not sacrificed.

candidates.name: coord-wave-strengthen-bath
candidates.hypothesis: The two heaviest arterial approaches (B_ATH Beaver EB 8365 s/ep with 89 s/ep spillback, C_ATH College WB 7387 s/ep) are limited by a weak coordination window bonus (6 ≈ only 6 queued vehicles) and B_ATH's low phase-0 cap (40 s), so during bursty platoons the controller switches away mid-platoon. Strengthening the arterial windows and raising B_ATH phase-0 capacity lets platoons clear, cutting the dominant stopped time and the bursty tail.
candidates.explanation: Keeps the champion's adaptive logic, weights, and offsets. Changes: (1) all six coordination windows length 30->36 s and bonus 6->10, so the arterial phase-0 green is held more firmly while a platoon is discharging (targets bursty scenarios where queues exceed the weak bonus); (2) B_ATH maxGreen phase0 40->48 s, letting the single heaviest approach (Beaver EB, 89 s/ep spillback) discharge oversized platoons per cycle instead of paying 5 s clearance + 2 s startup repeatedly. No changes to side-street weights, so side P95 should be roughly preserved.

candidates.hypothesis: Side-street tails (Allen/Pugh, 1 lane, 14-veh storage) are only served when the 90 s starvation rule fires, because oldestWait=0.04 contributes <2 points even after a 40 s wait; a moderate, per-intersection oldestWait raise at the four side-street nodes serves starved side queues ~20 s earlier, and a slightly larger hysteresis cuts the 5 s clearance + 2 s startup loss per switch under bursts, lowering both side and overall P95 without handing arterial green away in normal conditions.

Giving those two nodes long, stable holds (minHold 22, maxGreen 55/45, hysteresis 8) lets them clear bursts with fewer clearance penalties, while the four lighter side-street nodes keep short holds (minHold 14, hysteresis 7) so Allen/Pugh NB are served quickly and side P95 does not degrade.

(4) Coordination kept identical (cycle 95, six phase-0 arterial windows) so the successful College/Beaver wave is preserved; only per-intersection green-holding changes. Expected: lower arterial stopped time in bursty scenarios, side-street P95 held by the short holds at light nodes.
